Q1: A huge fire (the Great Fire, dated 2 Sept 1666) burns through a crowded city of timber houses beside a river. The fire spreads for days, with dates counting from 2 to 5 Sept 1666.
Q2: It seems to start in one small place. A baker's shop (Thomas Farriner, baker to the King) shows a glowing oven and sparks, and the fire then catches in a narrow street. After that it spreads across a big stretch of the riverside city, with smoke over the old London Bridge area. The pictures do not show the exact starting spot, so I am not sure of that.
Q3: People pack bundles and loaded carts and flee along the streets. Others row away on the river in boats with their goods. Men pull down houses with hooks and ropes, and one house is blown up, to make firebreaks. A Lord Mayor and a diarist appear as officials and witnesses. One pair bury valuables in a garden pit, and refugees camp in fields with tents and bundles outside the burning city.
Q4: The big Gothic church on the hill (shown on the 4 Sept frames, marked as Old St Paul's) catches fire. Its windows blaze, and what looks like molten lead streams down the walls and runs across the street. It is burned and ruined, and a statue lies among the rubble afterwards.
Q5: The city is rebuilt in red brick. Frames show brick houses going up with bricklayers, scaffolding and carts. The caption says 'Rebuilding on the old streets', so the old street pattern is kept and the rebuilt streets follow the old map. A hearing with judges and plans seems to be about the rebuilding, but I am not sure.
Q6: A large white cathedral with a big dome (St Paul's, 1708–1711) rises above the red-roofed houses. The caption says 'The dome rules the skyline', and a '365 ft' label appears. A tall column or monument also appears in the pictures, but I am not sure which frame shows it clearly.
Q7: On 29 Dec 1940 aircraft or airships fly over and the city burns again at night (a 'second great fire'). Firefighters work on the riverbank and on rooftops. A 'killed' counter (160) appears, and a large area is shown burned, with the 1941 map marking the damaged zone. The dome of St Paul's survives, shown with a ring around it in 1938 and in the snowy 1942 photo. The streets are rebuilt again on the same layout (1946, 'Second rebuilding, same streets').
Q8: Today (2026) it is a dense modern city of grey and brick office and apartment blocks and glass skyscrapers beside the river, with bridges. The dome of St Paul's can still be seen among the towers. The old street layout is still there, and the film ends by cutting back to the 1666 fire and to text about how it was made.
